_doc: Episode: The day and the week. One entry per scene; each language is a list of sentences (cues). Numbers in words, no exclamation marks. Narrate with the canvas-video skill: narrate.py website/video/day-and-week

en: How to read your plates, one day at a time, and seven at once.
Today is a stack of bands, one for each plate.
Four dyed stripes name the groups on it: veg and fruit, protein, starch and dairy.
A group that is not there stays bare cotton, a dashed line, never a warning.
A meal still to come is an open band, with nothing logged yet.
Tap a band to open its plate.
Each food is listed with its weight, in grams.
Below, each nutrient is a calm bar against the EU reference intake, or against your daily guide, if you fill in the optional profile.
Sugars and saturates sit indented, under carbohydrate and fat.
And when some foods have no data, a sentence says what the total is based on.
If numbers about food feel stressful, turn off Show nutrition numbers, in Settings.
The values and bars go away. Your meals and their weights stay.
This week hangs seven towels side by side, one for each day.
A plain sentence says which groups showed up, and which stayed quiet.
Below come the daily averages, and the days, one by one.
No scores, no streaks, nothing in the red.
The guide, Your day and your week, has the details.
